newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end near lows on technical selling.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end near lows on technical selling.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures finished near session lows Monday, suppressed by technical selling after two weeks of rallying and a drop in cash prices below December indices, industry sources said.

January, which reached a low of $3.21 earlier in the session, settled 25.1 cents lower at $3.246 per million British thermal units. February ended down 17 cents at $2.886, while other deferreds were also mostly lower.
In the ACCESS session, January remained fairly steady, trading around $3.22-3.23 early.
The next stop for January if the technical selling continues, traders say, is $3.04, a low set on November 21.
Resistance was pegged first around $3.40, then $3.44. Further resistance was seen in the $3.59-3.60 area, then at the $3.68 contract high.

In the cash market, prices on the Gulf Coast fell more than 10 cents to the high-$3.60s to about $3.70. Midcontinent prices slipped into the mid-$3.50s, while Rockies prices softened into the $3.30s, traders said.
The culprit was the mild weather stretched across many parts of the U.S., sources said.

However, historically-low storage inventories continue to support the market in the near-term, traders said, adding that the cash market's approximately 50-cent premium to Jan futures gives additional support.
NYMEX said an estimated 26,266 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 13,653. The 12-month strip dropped eight cents to $2.412.
NYMEX Alberta natgas futures, which traded only twice today, finished 10 cents higher at $1.70 in January. February ended up 11 cents at $1.60 after hitting a new contract high of $1.63.
In contrast, physical prices fell into the C$1.90-1.95 per gigajoule range, or the low-$1.50s per mmBtu.
NYMEX Permian natgas remained untraded, as January settled unchanged at $3.05.
Cash prices in the Permian basin were talked in the mid-$3.50s.
KCBT's January contract settled 19 cents lower at $3.12 after dipping to a session low of $3.07. The East/West spread narrowed by 6.1 cents to 12.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
